title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum at Lima Public Library
description:
Come sign the petition for SB1 Referendum at the **Lima Public Library** this Saturday from 9am-12pm.

## WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?

- Senate Bill 1  (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
- SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
- SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
- SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
- We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
- Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
- For more information, visit [ohiosb1petition.com](ohiosb1petition.com)
- Sign the petition to repeal SB1!

title: Invasive Vine Removal at Sligo Creek

sponsor.name: Chesapeake Climate Action Network / Action Fund

description:
Join CCAN and Friends of Sligo Creek to remove Invasive Vines along Sligo Creek in Hyattsville, MD.

We will meet along Sligo Creek (exact GPS coordinates will be emailed to participants) at 9am and work until about 11am. We will focus on non-native invasive vines including porcelainberry (Ampelopsis glandulosa var. brevipedunculata), English ivy (Hedera helix), and Kudzu (pueraria montana). Native Virginia creeper and poison ivy are also present and beneficial, so we will avoid those.

Please wear long pants, long sleeves, and close-toed shoes. Instructions and tools will be provided, so just bring yourself and a good attitude!

A reminder email will be sent out the day before with detailed instructions on where to meet.

title: Winston-Salem Screening of American Coup: Wilmington 1898
description:
We invite you to join Democracy North Carolina, The NAACP Winston-Salem Branch, Goler Memorial AME Zion Church Women’s Ministry, PBS North Carolina, and Working Films for a screening of *American Coup: Wilmington 1898* on **Friday, June 20th, from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM**. 

**This in-person event will take place at Goler Memorial AME Zion Church (3894 Northampton Dr, Winston-Salem, NC 27105).**

The event will begin promptly at 5:30 PM with a light reception. The film screening will start at 6:00 PM, followed by a panel discussion, audience Q&A, and a closing prayer.

*American Coup: Wilmington 1898* is a documentary that tells the little-known story of a deadly race massacre and a carefully orchestrated insurrection in North Carolina’s largest city in 1898 — the only coup d’état in US history.

The film shares the story of how self-described white supremacists used intimidation and violence to destroy Black political and economic power and overthrow Wilmington’s democratically elected, multi-racial government. Black residents were murdered, and thousands were banished. The story of what happened in Wilmington was suppressed for decades until descendants and scholars began to investigate. Today, many of those descendants — Black and white — seek the truth about this intentionally buried history.

We hope you join us for this free screening and discussion to learn more about the massacre and coup, its place in US history, and its lasting impact. 

Together, we can ensure that the lessons of Wilmington’s past inform conversations around democracy today.

Questions? Contact Linda at linda@democracync.org.

title: Phoenixville Dems Table at Juneteenth Celebrations
description:
The Phoenixville Dems will be setting up a table at the Juneteenth celebrations in Phoenixville!

Juneteenth National Freedom Day illuminates the fact that slaves celebrated the abolishment of slavery with excitement and great joy. It is a reminder to all Americans of the status and importance of Americans of African descent as American citizens. For more than 140 years, Juneteenth National Freedom Day has been the oldest African American holiday observed in the United States.

Juneteenth celebrations began in Phoenixville in 2002, experienced a hiedas and returned in to our community in 2021 with a week-long series of virtual events that were educational, entertaining, and inspirational!

This year on Sunday, June 22, between 2 and 6 pm, the Phoenixville Juneteenth Committee (Black Light Projects , Diversity In Action, Orion Communities, The Colonial Theatre, and the Phoenixville Community Health Foundation) has organized a special collection of activities to engage the community and shed light on the importance of African American history in the United States and our community. We will commemorate this important date with historical re-enactors, music, art, dance, drummers, street theater, magic, Soul food, and storytelling. The events will take place on the 200 block of Bridge Street in Phoenixville.

description:

What are we fighting for?

What do we bring?

	The goal is to be comfortable for the one hour we plan to be demonstrating. Please use your best judgement on what would be appropriate for this peaceful event. Some ideas of what could make it on your packing list to bring:  a friend, your family, a sign that shows why you are attending(slogan ideas to follow), a water source, a lawn chair.

Where should we park?
	
	Please use public parking along Main street and Buffalo street. If you know anyone in the neighborhood, you could ask to park at their house. If you are physically able, consider walking. 

Where are we meeting?
	
	We will congregate in front of the Marion Town Hall and will populate the corner of Main Street/Buffalo Street. We will not block any streets or sidewalks. All roadways and walkways will remain accessible and open. No businesses will be blocked including any buildings we may find ourselves in front of. Please be mindful of making room for others using the public space who are not a part of this demonstration. 

What do we do when we get there?

	Event Organizers will make an introduction and speak on behalf of the cause. Among the group we encourage you to share your story, share with others why you're here or why this is important to you or for the town of Marion. We aren't gathering just to stand against oligarchy, we are building community and that takes vulnerability. If you feel awkward or embarrassed, please know you're not the only one! Showing up takes guts and humility. Being afraid is the first step to being brave and your courage will not go unnoticed by your community! We are stronger together. 

Following the protest we encourage you to shop Main street, visit the park or cemetery or stop into the Marion Public Library prior to our demonstration. Enjoy what Marion has to offer,  we want to make a statement of investing into our community!

What if this event escalates negatively? 

	Our event organizers will participate in training that will help them mitigate any negative incidents. The most important thing to remember is that you cannot control anyone's actions but your own. Remain peaceful, do not engage with counter-protesters, and follow the directions and leadership of event organizers.

https://act.aclu.org/a/2025-kyr-training-2?/utm_source=email&source=nokingshostemail

No Kings Since 1776
Marion says No Kings!
The People United Can Never be Defeated
Oligarchy (with an X through the word) 
Money for Medicaid not Parades
For Democracy! No Kings.
Liberty and Justice for ALL

There should be nothing vulgar and no offensive language, please always defer to our base rules of peace and respect. No insults, slurs, bad jokes, or any other negative leaning statement or image.
